```{=html}
<p id="welcome" class="unnumbered" style="font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; margin: 1.1rem 0 1rem;">Welcome</p>

<div class="abstract-section">
  <div class="abstract-content">
    <p>Machine learning systems are computer systems whose behavior is learned from data rather than written by hand. Building one means engineering the data that trains the model, the algorithms that define it, and the machines that run it as a single design, because a weakness in any one of them limits the whole. Progress in machine learning has come mostly from general methods that improve as data and computation grow, so the system that carries a model increasingly decides what the model can achieve.</p>
    <p>This book develops these principles on a single machine, where every constraint is visible and measurable. It covers how deployment settings, from datacenter to microcontroller, set budgets for memory, power, and response time, and how data engineering bounds what a model can learn. It follows a model from mathematics to hardware through neural computation, architectures, frameworks, and training. It then treats optimization through data selection, model compression, and hardware acceleration, with benchmarking to verify each gain, and closes with serving, operations, and responsible engineering in production.</p>
  </div>
```

<p id="learning-path" class="unnumbered" style="font-size: 1.45rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25; margin: 1.5rem 0 0.75rem;">Learning Path</p>

The book progresses through four stages:

- **Part I: Foundations.** What is being built, under which physical constraints, across which lifecycle stages, and from what engineered data pipelines.
- **Part II: Development.** How mathematical models reach hardware execution, through neural computation, model architectures, frameworks, and single-node training loops.
- **Part III: Optimization.** How data selection, model compression, and hardware acceleration reduce system cost, and how benchmarking verifies each claimed speedup.
- **Part IV: Deployment.** How the system serves live requests under strict latency budgets, how monitoring catches silent drift and skew in production, and how responsible engineering controls are enforced.

<p id="prerequisites" class="unnumbered" style="font-size: 1.45rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25; margin: 1.5rem 0 0.75rem;">Prerequisites</p>

Readers should bring two core prerequisites, along with helpful background developed in the text:

- **Programming proficiency**: Fluency in Python, including familiarity with NumPy array manipulation.
- **Mathematics foundations**: Comfort with undergraduate linear algebra, calculus, and probability.
- **Machine learning context**: Prior ML exposure is helpful but not required; @sec-neural-computation builds the modeling foundations from first principles.

```{=html}
<script>
async function fetchGitHubStars() {
  const starElement = document.getElementById('star-count');

  try {
    const response = await fetch('https://api.github.com/repos/harvard-edge/cs249r_book');
    const data = await response.json();
    const starCount = data.stargazers_count;
    const formattedCount = starCount.toLocaleString();
    starElement.textContent = formattedCount;
    starElement.style.opacity = '1';
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to fetch GitHub stars:', error);
    starElement.textContent = 'Unavailable';
    starElement.style.opacity = '1';
  }
}

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', fetchGitHubStars);
</script>
```
